\begin{lemma}[Primitive cuts and determinant recursion] \label{f9mi:primitivecut} Assume $r\geq1$. There is an $R$-basis $e_0,\ldots,e_r$ of $E$ with $u(e_0)=1$ and $E'=\ker u=Re_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Re_r$. The horizontal model cut is $\mathbf P(E')\simeq\mathbf P_R^{r-1}$. For $r\geq1$, a section $s=\ell^m$ with metric shift $c$ and clearing exponent $e$ as above has normalized model divisor \begin{equation}\label{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:divisor} \frac1e\cyc\bigl(\divi_{\cO(em)}(s^{\otimes e})\bigr) =m[\mathbf P(E')]+(ma+c)[V]. \end{equation} The generic divisor is $m[\mathbf P(E'_K)]$. A negative $ma+c$ is allowed as a rational vertical coefficient. All coefficients are computed by ordinary algebraic DVR orders, with actual quotient lengths.
If $\ell=\ell_i$ is a row of an invertible $(r+1)$-row matrix $A$, the other rows restrict to an invertible $r$-row matrix $A_i$ on $E'_K$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:detrec} v(\det A)=a_i+v(\det A_i). \end{equation} The restricted standard metric is the standard metric for the lattice $E'$, with the same shift $c_j$ and exponent $m_j$ for every remaining line. No primitivity of these restricted rows is assumed. \end{lemma} \F9MIProofInputs{Elementary integral row reduction; ordinary DVR length convention of NAG-002552. The proof does not invoke the pending model log/divisor packet or a general intersection product.} \begin{proof} Permute the coordinates to make a unit coefficient first, divide that coordinate vector by the unit, and subtract multiples of it from the other coordinate vectors. These are invertible $R$-operations and give the displayed basis. The content is the fractional ideal generated by the row coefficients, so this ideal and $a$ are invariant under an invertible $R$-basis change. The primitive equation is now $z_0=0$. Its model quotient is a polynomial projective hyperplane over $R$, which proves the claim about $\mathbf P(E')$.
In a model frame, the coefficient of $s^{\otimes e}$ has a factor $\pi^{e(ma+c)}u^{em}$. At the generic point of the horizontal hyperplane its order is $em$, and at the generic point of $V$ its order is $e(ma+c)$. These are the only components of the divisor. At a DVR with parameter $t$, the successive powers in $A/(t^n)$ give length $n$; for a rational coefficient one subtracts the lengths of numerator and denominator. Thus no nilpotent layer in $u^{em}=0$ is removed. Divide the coefficients by $e$ to obtain \eqref{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:divisor}.
Move row $i$ to the first position and use the constructed basis. The matrix becomes \[ \begin{pmatrix}\pi^{a_i}&0\ *&A_i\end{pmatrix}. \] Row permutation and the basis matrix have determinant a unit up to sign, proving \eqref{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:detrec}; its nonzero determinant also proves that $A_i$ is invertible over $K$. Finally, a matrix in $\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}(R)$ and its inverse both have operator norm at most one for the maximum norm over every valued extension of $K$. Consequently the maximum norm is unchanged. Restriction to the direct summand $E'$ gives exactly the standard metric in its basis. \end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Atomic calibration on the projective model] \label{f9mi:atomiccalibration} For any set $J$ of $r$ remaining lines on $\mathbf P(E)$, the specified mixed model measure and its mass are \begin{equation}\label{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:one-atom} \mu_J=D_J\delta_{\xi_E},\qquad D_J=\prod_{j\in J}m_j =\deg_{(L_j)_{j\in J},K}(\mathbf P(E_K)). \end{equation} The empty product in dimension zero is one. For a further nonzero row $\ell_i$ of content $a_i$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:logterm} \int_{\mathbf P(E_K)^\an}-\log\|s_i\|_i\,d\mu_J =\lambda(m_i a_i+c_i)D_J. \end{equation} The logarithm is finite at the atom, and every proper algebraic closed subset has measure zero. For $r\geq1$ the normalized horizontal coefficient is $m_i$. For $r=0$ the generic divisor is empty and the horizontal part is zero. The normalized vertical coefficient is $m_i a_i+c_i$, and the special-fibre multiplicity is one. There is no additional factorial. \end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetric projective model induction] \label{f9mi:symmetricinduction} The recursion is defined at every stage for every permutation of the indices. Every order gives \begin{equation}\label{eq:ex68:f9mi-projective:height-formula} H_E=\lambda\left(D\,v(\det A) +\sum_{i=0}^r c_i\frac{D}{m_i}\right), \qquad D=\prod_{i=0}^r m_i. \end{equation} It is therefore symmetric in the labelled pairs $(L_i,s_i)$, independent of the chosen integral bases and primitive complements, and independent of the clearing exponents $e_i$. The value changes by $\lambda q D/m_i$ if $c_i$ is increased by $q\in\mathbf Q$. Replacing $\ell_i$ by $b_i\ell_i$, $b_i\in K^\times$, changes the value by $-D\sum_i\log|b_i|$.
This is a self-contained model recursion on the stated projective class. It identifies the restriction of the primary BPS induction to this class because its base value, divisor cycle and measure are the same. No native smooth-integral comparison, analytic adjointness, metric limit, model-change invariance or extension to arbitrary pseudo-divisors is part of the assertion. \end{theorem}

Compute the mixed degree and specialize the model weight at the Gauss atom. The Gauss seminorm evaluates the row by its coefficient content. Additional hypotheses: The printed projective DVR and root-metric data An explicit model measure supported at the unit Gauss point, with reduced special component of multiplicity one.

Substitute the atom calibration into the recursion. The primitive-cut determinant recurrence identifies the value for each first index. Additional hypotheses: The printed projective DVR model and root metrics All supplied datum, divisor, measure and dimension-zero conditions remain in force.
